title: Grant recommendation intake, affirmation and duplicate detection
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-001, UNB-GRANT-002, UNB-GRANT-029, UNB-RCN-GRT-010); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: A grant recommendation is a typed request that captures recommender, fund, recipient identity, purpose, amount, timing, restrictions and recognition preference, together with an affirmation evidence record (presented disclosure text and hash, the donor's no-benefit and no-pledge certifications, channel, time and idempotency key). Submission never creates an entitlement or moves money. Duplicate and replayed submissions are handled idempotently, and suspicious repeated or split recommendations are flagged across channels.

title: Grant approval workflow, board-delegated policy approval and segregation of duties
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-001, UNB-GRANT-012, UNB-GRANT-013, CNV-GRT-011); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Approval authority derives from a recorded sponsor board or committee resolution. Until such a resolution adopts a version-pinned policy and names a delegate, deterministic policy only recommends and an accountable person decides. Once delegated, conforming items may be approved by policy under the delegate's authority, while exceptions and enhanced-review triggers route to qualified humans by amount, risk and relationship. The engine enforces segregation of duties, vendor staff and AI agents cannot hold approval authority, decision quality is checked by risk-stratified sampling, and approval atomically reserves the approved amount.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound is requirements-only with no production system, customers or operating evidence (unbound@9b38de47).
intended_practice: Policy-delegation model per CNV-GRT-001, routing per UNB-GRANT-012 and CNV-GRT-011, authority per CNV-GOV-003/004/010, reservation per CNV-FIN-001.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text exists in unbound@9b38de47 (requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl); no implementation, test execution or operating evidence.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors want every grant to be properly authorized and reviewed so that charitable assets are protected.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An improper or fraudulent grant is paid; sponsor faces excise tax, loss or reputational harm.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Human review of every routine grant to a verified public charity adds delay and fatigue; reviewers rubber-stamp high volumes, so marginal detection is low.
challenge.legally_required: No statute requires human review of each grant; the sponsor must exercise exclusive legal control, which board delegation can satisfy.
challenge.contractually_required: Some sponsor policies and bank-affiliated sponsor procedures require dual human approval.
challenge.historical_convention: Program officers or grant administrators approve each grant, often with a second approver above a threshold.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Deterministic gates eliminate entire classes of ineligible grants (revoked charities, natural persons, sanctioned recipients) before any human sees them.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Board-adopted policy approves only conforming items; exceptions route to humans.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Each approval records the policy version and delegation; sampling measures error rates with stated bounds.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Deterministic gates plus delegated policy approval and risk-stratified sampling.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via replay and sampling results; independent verification requires an external examination.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain: national sponsors already use automation; community foundations and bank-affiliated sponsors may insist on human approval.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If eligibility data is stale or the policy is mis-specified, automation approves errors at scale.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium build cost, low recurring cost.
challenge.alternative_risks: Systematic error propagation; regulators or auditors unfamiliar with policy approval may object.
supporting_arguments: Concentrates human attention on real risk
opposing_arguments: Board must understand what it delegated

title: Grant purpose, restrictions, agreements and post-approval modification
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-010, UNB-GRANT-024, UNB-GRANT-048, CNV-GRT-008); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Grant purposes and restrictions are structured data evaluated against sponsor, program and fund policy in explicit precedence order. Restrictions that would deliver a benefit to the donor or name a foreign organization through an intermediary are blocked or routed for review. Grant agreements, milestones and reporting obligations are supported for conditional grants. Material modifications after approval (recipient, amount, purpose, timing, restrictions) require re-evaluation and human approval.

title: Recurring and scheduled grants with per-instance re-evaluation
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-003, UNB-GRANT-027, TVR-GR-005, TVR-GR-008); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Each instance of a recurring or scheduled grant re-checks the template author's current authority, the recipient's eligibility and sanctions status, fund availability and current sponsor policy at execution, and reserves individually. Series are paused, not silently skipped, on failure; changes in purpose, class or eligibility require reconfirmation, and series affected by a recipient merger carry a notice-and-opt-out window.

title: Pledges, event benefits and other prohibited benefit scenarios
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-010, UNB-RCN-GRT-012, UNB-GRANT-011, CNV-GRT-009); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Pledge handling is an explicit sponsor policy choice (Prohibited, NonBindingOnly, or conditions consistent with IRS Notice 2017-73 section 7). Embedded and API giving requests declare a typed host context (donation, event ticket, sponsorship, auction, membership with benefits), and benefit-bearing contexts are rejected or routed to the benefit gate. Grants are blocked to purposes that provide tuition, memberships with more than incidental benefits, or tickets, and bifurcated grants (DAF pays the charitable portion, donor pays the benefit) follow sponsor policy.

title: Neutral decline reasons and independent reconsideration
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-012, UNB-GRANT-037, UNB-GRT-002, UNB-GRANT-028); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Declines use a sponsor-configurable neutral catalog: donor-facing text describes the policy outcome, never facts about a charity; sanctions, investigation and law-enforcement reasons map to a generic compliance review code; charity-facing communication is limited to status codes. Reconsideration defaults to a 60-day filing window and a 30-day response target, is decided by a reviewer independent of the original decision, and both records survive with outcomes Upheld, Reversed, Modified, Withdrawn or Referred.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors want to explain declines to donors without defaming charities or tipping off subjects of investigations.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Defamation claims, tipping off in sanctions or law enforcement matters, or donor complaints of arbitrary treatment.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Free-text decline notes written by staff are inconsistent and risky.
challenge.legally_required: No statute prescribes decline wording; tipping-off and defamation risk arise from general law.
challenge.historical_convention: Staff write ad hoc decline emails.
challenge.architectural_elimination: A closed catalog of neutral codes removes the possibility of factual allegations in donor-facing text.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Only catalog phrases can be sent; free text limited to approved phrases.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every decline carries its code and reviewer, enabling consistency analysis.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Donors may perceive neutral codes as evasive, increasing reconsideration volume.
challenge.conventional_cost: Low cost, high latent legal risk.
supporting_arguments: Removes defamation and tipping-off risk structurally
opposing_arguments: Some sponsors want to give donors richer explanations

title: Payee substitution, payment destination integrity and partner exclusion from funds flow
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-007, CNV-GRT-010, UNB-GEX-018, CNV-PAY-002); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Canonical charity identity, legal payee, fiscal sponsor, project and payment destination are resolved separately. Payee substitution to a merger successor requires a verified legal successor passing eligibility on its own EIN in the same recipient class, sponsor approval and donor notice. Bank-detail changes require independent verification (bank-originated account owner match, cooling-off, notice to old and new verified channels) and dual control, and unverified changes cannot propagate into approved payment instructions. No partner, host or vendor account ever appears in the payment path.

title: Returned, uncashed and refunded grant payments
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-022, UNB-GRANT-028, TVR-GR-002, UNB-PAY-006); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Payment states distinguish prepared, approved, submitted, accepted, rejected, settled, returned and reconciled. Returns after disbursement are accepted and restore the fund through linked reversal entries, uncashed checks follow a sponsor-approved aging and reissue or redirect policy that considers state unclaimed property rules, and grantee refunds are recorded as linked corrections with donor notice. Unknown payment outcomes are never treated as failures without proof.

title: Grant anonymity and recognition preferences
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-GRANT-025, UNB-GRANT-002, ADM-013, UNB-XIN-EVA-014); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Each grant carries a recognition election (full name, name only, custom attribution, fund name only, anonymous), stored as an authority fact with effective time. Correspondence, remittance data and payment references are derived from the election at send time; immediately before external send the delivery worker re-reads the current election and suppresses or regenerates the message if it changed. Anonymity applies to charities and partners but does not prevent sponsor compliance screening or legally required disclosure.
